title: Pre-trade limits, kill switches and invariants
objectives: Reserve potential open-order cash and position exposure together before admitting a new command, checking exact units, bounds, existing-state consistency and aggregate invariants.

Separate disabling new risk, cancel requests and reconciled cancellation; reject unavailable or stale control inputs without pretending a pure candidate is a concurrent, durable or live risk-control system.
Apply pre-trade limits, kill switches and invariants invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: Risk checks belong before routing a new order, not in an after-the-fact warning that assumes cancellation will beat execution. As a scoped US securities example, SEC Rule 15c3-5 concerns broker-dealers with market access and controls reasonably designed to reject orders beyond appropriate credit/capital thresholds or erroneous-order parameters.

blocks.md: Risk checks belong before routing a new order, not in an after-the-fact warning that assumes cancellation will beat execution. As a scoped US securities example, SEC Rule 15c3-5 concerns broker-dealers with market access and controls reasonably designed to reject orders beyond appropriate credit/capital thresholds or erroneous-order parameters. Its staff FAQ distinguishes pre-entry prevention from chase-and-cancel. This is not legal advice, a universal rule for every jurisdiction/product, or a claim our educational model meets the rule. Real thresholds require appropriate business judgment, aggregate coverage, review and supervisory ownership.

Use one currency in integer minor units and one long-only instrument. cash is current unspent cash before subtracting open BUY reservations; position is already owned units. Each open reservation (id, limit_price, remaining_qty) includes outstanding possible buys, including sent-but-unconfirmed or cancel-pending quantity when that outcome is unresolved. The own zero-fee upper-bound invariants are sum(price*qty)<=cash and position+sum(qty)<=cap. Reserving only filled quantities ignores the future exposure of working orders. Do not offset possible buys with unconfirmed sells.

blocks.title: Two individually affordable orders can breach aggregate limits
items: Cash 1000 minor units, position 2, cap 10. Existing BUY 3 at 100 reserves 300 cash and 3 possible units: available 700; potential position 5.
New BUY 4 at 100 brings cash reservation 700 and potential position 9, so this toy can reserve it. The candidate still has 1000 unspent cash; 700 is reserved, not spent. No order is sent.

Another BUY 2 at 100 would bring potential position 11>10 and is rejected despite costing only 200. Disabling new orders preserves the existing 700 reservation; it does not prove those 7 units cannot fill.

blocks.code:
def admit_buy(cash,position,cap,open_orders,request,enabled,age_ms):
    # Own long-only, one-instrument, one-currency, zero-fee BUY reservation model.
    for value,upper in ((cash,10**9),(position,1000),(cap,1000),(age_ms,10**6)):
        if type(value) is not int or not 0<=value<=upper:
            raise ValueError("invalid state scalar")
    if position>cap or type(enabled) is not bool:
        raise ValueError("invalid position or gate")
    if type(open_orders) is not tuple or len(open_orders)>16:
        raise ValueError("invalid bounded reservation list")
    def valid_order(order):
        return (type(order) is tuple and len(order)==3 and
                all(type(x) is int for x in order) and
                1<=order[0]<=10000 and 1<=order[1]<=10000 and 1<=order[2]<=100)
    if not all(valid_order(o) for o in open_orders) or not valid_order(request):
        raise ValueError("invalid order fields")
    ids=[o[0] for o in open_orders]
    if len(set(ids))!=len(ids) or request[0] in ids:
        raise ValueError("duplicate live reservation identity")
    reserved=sum(price*qty for _,price,qty in open_orders)
    exposure=position+sum(qty for _,_,qty in open_orders)
    if reserved>cash or exposure>cap:
        raise ValueError("inconsistent existing reservations")
    if not enabled:return "disabled",open_orders
    if age_ms>100:return "stale",open_orders
    if len(open_orders)==16:return "capacity",open_orders
    _,price,qty=request
    if exposure+qty>cap:return "position",open_orders
    if reserved+price*qty>cash:return "cash",open_orders
    return "reserved",open_orders+(request,)

original=((1,100,3),)
status,candidate=admit_buy(1000,2,10,original,(2,100,4),True,100)
print(status,candidate)
print(admit_buy(1000,2,10,candidate,(3,100,2),True,0)[0])
print(admit_buy(1000,2,10,candidate,(3,100,1),False,0))
print(original)
blocks.caption: Expected lines: reserved ((1, 100, 3), (2, 100, 4)); position; ('disabled', ((1, 100, 3), (2, 100, 4))); ((1, 100, 3),). Own exact-int bounds: cash 0..1e9, position/cap 0..1000, order price 1..10000, qty 1..100, id 1..10000, <=16 live reservations; age 0..1e6 ms with 100 ms inclusive fresh. Schema errors raise ValueError; control rejections return reason and same immutable reservations. No fee, short, sell, margin, FX, price-band, rate-limit or live-send implementation.

blocks.md: The disabled and stale results deny this new BUY only. Malformed, missing or inconsistent state raises an error and must be routed into a blocked/unavailable control state, not caught and interpreted as permission. age_ms is a supplied bounded age value, not proof of a current authenticated clock/feed. Production freshness must bind source/session and monotonic receipt timing with an explicit policy for gaps, clock jumps and unknown input. Our threshold 100 ms is invented for traceable exercises, not a recommended latency limit.

After a confirmed partial fill of q at execution price e<=reserved limit p, reduce unspent cash by e*q, increase position by q, and reduce that order remaining by q in one coherent update;reserved amount drops p*q. Under the zero-fee assumptions,free cash increases by (p-e)*q and position+remaining exposure is unchanged. A confirmed cancel releases only the unfilled reservation; cancel request alone releases nothing. Rejection, replace, correction, fees, FX and uncertain reconnect outcomes need explicit events/reconciliation. The function only admits reservations; it does not implement these lifecycle transitions or persist/reconcile IDs.

Define scope and acknowledgment for every kill mechanism: local new-order gate, venue session disconnect, order cancellation and account/firm-wide blocking are different actions. Keep cancel/reconcile handling available through an appropriately controlled path while blocking new risk; do not blindly route cancels through a BUY admission gate. CME Direct documents Kill my orders as your entered orders, not all company orders. No universal kill label proves every venue/order is canceled. Record what was requested, acknowledged, still working and unknown; fills that race a cancel remain real exposure.

Two workers can each read available cash 700, each accept a 500 reservation, and jointly over-reserve. Run validate-check-reserve in one serialized/transactional revision-checked state transition; on conflict reload and recheck rather than publishing both candidates. A pure function protects caller input and yields a candidate, but it cannot atomically publish it to concurrent senders or bind reservation+durable command intent+remote acceptance. A timeout after send requires reconciliation, not automatic release of reserved exposure. Never use this lesson as authority to send a live order.

Independent transfer: test exact-limit acceptance, one-above rejection, aggregate open orders, stale age 100 versus 101, disabled with existing reservations, zero cash, duplicate live IDs, malformed bools and 16-slot capacity. Construct two accepted candidates from the same old state whose union breaches cash, then explain the required concurrency boundary. Add a fill/cancel reducer only after specifying its event identity, fees, source and coherent cash/position/reservation update; do not erase unknown exposure to make the invariant appear green.

Sources: [SEC market-access rule overview](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/2011/06/risk-management-controls-brokers-or-dealers-market-access), [SEC staff FAQ including Question 16](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/trading-markets-frequently-asked-questions/divisionsmarketregfaq-0), [CME Direct holding/killing scope](https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/webhelp/cme-direct/cme-direct-trader-broker/Content/HeldOrders.html), [Azure event-store optimistic concurrency discussion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/event-sourcing). Staff FAQ is staff guidance, not a new Commission rule. All concrete model limits and gate/reason order here are own teaching policy.

guidedExercise.prompt: After send timeout and then a local kill-toggle, why must unresolved order exposure remain visible?
hints: Separates timeout/local gate from remote outcome.
Retains unresolved exposure pending source evidence.
guidedExercise.solution: The remote order may have been accepted/filled despite timeout. A local new-risk gate proves no cancellation. Keep reservations/unknown status, source-bound events, cancel acknowledgments and reconciliation; allow controlled cancel/reconcile work and block new uncertain risk. Need coherent durable/concurrent state, not a green local flag.

hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: Sum current holdings and possible remaining buys under the declared one-instrument model. (Do not release cancel-pending or unknown exposure merely on local intent.)
New-risk blocking is narrower than venue cancellation or full-account safety. (Cancellation and reconciliation are separate workflows.)
3*100+4*100=700; unspent cash stays 1000 until actual fills.
realWorldApplication: In practice, engineering teams apply pre-trade limits, kill switches and invariants within Market Data and Execution Systems when building reliable trading systems and low latency workflows — specifically to reserve potential open-order cash and position exposure together before admitting a new command, checking exact units, bounds, existing-state consistency and aggregate invariants.
quantFinanceApplication: Desk workflows in Market Data and Execution Systems rely on pre-trade limits, kill switches and invariants across trading systems, low latency, microstructure, keeping numerical estimates, risk bounds, and low-latency paths predictable.
summary: Aggregate possible open-order exposure matters before routing.
Check and reserve together, retain unresolved/cancel-pending exposure, and distinguish blocking new commands from confirmed cancel/reconciliation.
This pure zero-fee long-only candidate is not a concurrent, durable or regulatory-complete live risk engine.

quiz.prompt: Which quantity belongs in a conservative potential long-position check?
options: Owned units only, ignoring live buys
Owned units plus all possible remaining buy quantities
Owned units plus buys after subtracting all unconfirmed sell requests
quiz.explanation: Sum current holdings and possible remaining buys under the declared one-instrument model. (Do not release cancel-pending or unknown exposure merely on local intent.)

quiz.prompt: Disabling this toy BUY gate does what?
options: Confirms every company order is canceled
Allows a malformed order if it arrives fast
quiz.explanation: New-risk blocking is narrower than venue cancellation or full-account safety. (Cancellation and reconciliation are separate workflows.)

quiz.prompt: Cash 1000; existing BUY 3 at 100 and new BUY 4 at 100. What is total reserved cash in this zero-fee model?
quiz.explanation: 3*100+4*100=700; unspent cash stays 1000 until actual fills.

quiz.prompt: Two workers each accept a candidate from the same old available-cash snapshot. What is missing?
options: Publishing both individually valid candidates without checking their common base revision
An unbounded timestamp retry with no check
Automatic release of all unknown orders
quiz.explanation: Serialize or use a transaction/revision conflict protocol around the shared state transition. (Each candidate alone can be valid while their union breaches limits.)

quiz.prompt: Why is route-then-immediately-cancel not equivalent to rejecting an excessive order before routing?
options: Every cancellation is guaranteed faster than execution
The source event log becomes irrelevant
The cancel request reverses all past fills
Execution can occur before cancellation is confirmed
quiz.explanation: The SEC staff FAQ specifically rejects chase-and-cancel as the pre-entry prevention described there. (Prevention and later mitigation are different.)
